text.p: Lehman Brothers cut its 1997 earnings-per-share estimate for Lasmo Plc to 4.1p from 4.6p on Friday, the investment bank said.

Lehman analysts said the move was prompted by development delays at its MacCulloch oil field in the North Sea, higher interest charges due to bonus payments following the recent purchase of Venezuelan oil reserves, and the continuing strength of sterling.
Lehman repeated an "underperform" rating on the stock, saying it had spread itself too thin operationally and the stock was one of the most expensive in the sector.
They said Premier Oil Plc, unchanged at 46p, was their favourite play in the oil exploration sector.
On Thursday Dresdner Kleinwort Benson cut Lasmo to a "hold" from a "buy." The stock was up 3-1/2p at 267 by 0928 GMT.
